evals.prompt: Two things my design lead said that I need the right words for. First: 'the spring feels finished way before the numbers actually stop moving' — apparently that's a known concept? Second: what do you call that tiny wind-up move in the opposite direction right before something slides away — and how is it different from the thing where parts of the element keep drifting and settle a beat after the main motion stops?
evals.expected_output: Perceptual duration for the first. Anticipation for the wind-up, contrasted with follow-through for the post-motion settle, all three named with one-line definitions and disambiguated crisply.
expectations: Names 'perceptual duration' for a spring that feels finished while still micro-settling underneath
Names 'anticipation' for the small opposite-direction wind-up before the main motion
Names 'follow-through' for parts continuing to move and settling after the main motion stops, explicitly contrasted with anticipation (before vs after the main motion)
Stays in naming mode: leads with the terms and definitions, no implementation code

evals.prompt: What's the name for the technique where you measure where an element starts and ends, jump it to the end, then animate a transform back from the start? My skill list doesn't have it, I think.
evals.expected_output: FLIP (first, last, invert, play), named as the lead term with a one-line definition, even though the skill's own list does not carry it.
expectations: Names FLIP (first, last, invert, play) as the lead term
Does not refuse or hedge because the term is missing from the skill's list
Gives a correct one-line definition: measure first and last positions, invert with a transform, play the transform back to none
Keeps it to naming, with no implementation code

evals.prompt: My designer says our dashboard 'enters twice': the whole panel slides in, then every card inside it staggers in again. Is there a word for that, and is it a problem?
evals.expected_output: Layered entry, the house term for stacking a container entrance and a second entrance of its contents; the house rule is one entrance per container.
expectations: Names 'layered entry' as the lead term
Defines it as a container entrance followed by a second entrance of its contents
States the house rule: one entrance per container
Stays in naming mode and offers frontend-design at most once for the fix
